title: What are the AQF levels and how do learning outcomes differ between them?
description: The 10 AQF levels explained: qualification types, level criteria for knowledge, skills and application, volume of learning, and the new Vocational Degree.
shortAnswer: The Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) has 10 levels, from Certificate I at level 1 to the Doctoral Degree at level 10. Each level is defined by learning outcome criteria in three dimensions: knowledge, skills, and the application of knowledge and skills. Outcomes rise in complexity and depth, and in the autonomy and judgement a graduate must show, from routine work in stable contexts to original research at the frontier of a discipline.
keyTakeaways: The AQF Second Edition January 2013 is still the main policy document as at September 2026, amended by addenda rather than replaced.
Every level and qualification type is expressed as learning outcomes across knowledge, skills, and application of knowledge and skills.
Two qualification types were added or confirmed in 2025: the Undergraduate Certificate became permanent, and the Vocational Degree was created at level 7.
Volume of learning, expressed in equivalent full time years, sits alongside the level criteria to set the depth and breadth of a qualification.
The AQF is given regulatory force through accreditation: TEQSA for higher education and ASQA, VRQA or TAC for vocational education and training.
regulator: Department of Education (manages the AQF in consultation with the states and territories); applied through accreditation by TEQSA, ASQA, VRQA and WA TAC
appliesTo: Higher education providers and self accrediting universities
Registered training organisations and developers of training packages and accredited courses
Employers and professional bodies that specify qualification levels for roles

sections.heading: What is the AQF and who does it apply to?

blocks.text: The Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) is the national policy for regulated qualifications in Australian education and training, covering senior secondary, vocational education and training (VET), and higher education. The [AQF website](https://www.aqf.edu.au/) states that it "defines the essential characteristics, including the required learning outcomes, of the different types of qualifications" issued across those three sectors.

As at September 2026, the main policy document is still the [AQF Second Edition January 2013](https://www.aqf.edu.au/framework/australian-qualifications-framework). It has been amended through numbered addenda rather than replaced. The most recent are Addendum No. 5 (November 2024, Masters Degree (Extended) and the Issuance Policy), Addendum No. 6 (January 2025, the permanent Undergraduate Certificate) and Addendum No. 7 (February 2025, the Vocational Degree).

According to the [AQF governance page](https://www.aqf.edu.au/about/governance), the framework is managed by the Australian Government Department of Education in consultation with the states and territories. Changes are endorsed by Commonwealth, state and territory Education and Skills Ministers. The AQF Council was disbanded by ministers in 2014.

The AQF is policy, not legislation, but it binds providers through accreditation. For higher education, Standard 1.5.3 of the [Higher Education Standards Framework (Threshold Standards) 2021](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2021L00488/2026-07-14/2026-07-14/text/original/pdf) requires that "the learning outcomes for the qualification are consistent with the level classification for that qualification in the Australian Qualifications Framework". See [what the HESF requires of course design](/regulations/teqsa-hesf-course-design-requirements). For VET, qualifications are developed through training packages or accredited courses and delivered under the [2025 Standards for RTOs](/regulations/standards-for-rtos-2025-training-and-assessment).

sections.heading: How does the AQF define a level?

blocks.text: An AQF level is a statement of the relative complexity and depth of achievement, and the autonomy required to demonstrate it. Level 1 has the lowest complexity and level 10 the highest. The [AQF levels page](https://www.aqf.edu.au/framework/aqf-levels) describes the level summaries as "statements of the typical achievement of graduates" awarded a qualification at that level.

The AQF Second Edition expresses every level and every qualification type as [learning outcomes](/glossary/learning-outcomes), "what graduates are expected to know, understand and be able to do as a result of learning", in three dimensions:

items: **Knowledge**: what a graduate knows and understands, described by depth (general to specialised), breadth (a single topic to multidisciplinary), kind (concrete to abstract) and complexity.
**Skills**: what a graduate can do, including cognitive and creative, technical, communication, interpersonal and generic skills.

**Application of knowledge and skills**: the context in which a graduate applies them, expressed as autonomy, responsibility and accountability, in contexts ranging from predictable to unpredictable and tasks from routine to non routine.

blocks.text: The level criteria are written broadly so that more than one qualification type can sit at a level. The qualification type descriptor is more specific, which is why a Graduate Certificate and a Bachelor Honours Degree share level 8 but have different purposes and descriptors. The AQF also recognises four categories of generic learning outcomes: fundamental skills, people skills, thinking skills and personal skills.

sections.heading: What are the 10 AQF levels and qualification types?

blocks.text: The 10 levels run from Certificate I to the Doctoral Degree. VET qualifications span levels 1 to 8 and higher education spans levels 5 to 10, so Diplomas, Advanced Diplomas, Graduate Certificates and Graduate Diplomas can be issued in either sector. The summaries below are quoted from the [AQF levels criteria](https://www.aqf.edu.au/framework/aqf-levels); qualification types are from the [AQF qualifications page](https://www.aqf.edu.au/framework/aqf-qualifications); volume of learning is from the qualification type descriptors.

blocks.text: Two qualification types sit outside a single level. The Senior Secondary Certificate of Education is not located at any level (typically 2 years). The Undergraduate Certificate is not located at a particular level but draws its content from higher education units at levels 5, 6 or 7 (typically 0.5 years).

sections.heading: How do learning outcomes change from one level to the next?

blocks.text: Outcomes change in three predictable ways as the level rises: knowledge moves from factual and procedural to theoretical, integrated and then original; problems move from predictable to complex and unpredictable; and application moves from autonomy within narrow parameters to authoritative judgement as a leading practitioner or scholar. The phrases below are taken directly from the [AQF level criteria](https://www.aqf.edu.au/framework/aqf-levels).

blocks.text: The verbs matter. Level 5 skills include the ability to "analyse information"; level 7 adds "analyse and evaluate"; level 8 requires graduates to "analyse critically, evaluate and transform information"; level 9 requires them to "reflect on and synthesise complex information, problems, concepts and theories". This is close to the progression in [Bloom's taxonomy](/glossary/blooms-taxonomy), and it gives designers a defensible basis for choosing outcome verbs.

sections.heading: What does the same topic look like at different levels?

blocks.text: The same subject can be taught at almost any level; what changes is the outcome statement and the evidence that proves it. The example below is illustrative only, written for this page using the AQF level criteria. It is not taken from any accredited qualification or training package.

blocks.caption: Illustrative: one topic (workplace risk assessment) written as outcomes at four AQF levels, with matching assessment evidence
head: Level
Illustrative learning outcome
Assessment evidence that would demonstrate it
rows: Follow the organisation's procedure to identify hazards in a routine task and report them to a supervisor
Observed completion of a hazard checklist on a live task; supervisor sign off
Conduct a risk assessment for a range of work activities, select controls from the hierarchy of controls, and brief the team on them
Completed risk assessments for several activities; recorded team briefing; questioning on control selection
Analyse and evaluate risk across a work system, justify control strategies against legislation and standards, and advise managers on residual risk
Written analysis of a case site; justified recommendations report; oral defence
Critically evaluate risk assessment methods against research evidence, and design and justify a risk framework for a complex organisation
Research informed framework design; critical literature review; examined presentation to specialist and non specialist audiences

blocks.text: Two points follow. First, the evidence has to match the application dimension: a level 7 outcome cannot be proven by a checklist, because the criteria require judgement in self-directed contexts. Second, a program that claims a level must show the outcomes at that level are actually assessed. Mapping each outcome to a level criterion and an assessment task is the core of [writing measurable learning outcomes](/guides/how-to-write-measurable-learning-outcomes) and [building a curriculum map](/guides/how-to-build-a-curriculum-map).

sections.heading: What is volume of learning and how is it used?

blocks.text: Volume of learning is the notional duration of all activities needed to achieve a qualification's learning outcomes, expressed in equivalent full time years. It is a dimension of complexity used alongside the level criteria and qualification type descriptor, not a measure of seat time.
The AQF's [Volume of Learning: An Explanation](https://www.aqf.edu.au/publication/volume-learning-v2-2014) sets out the working rules:

items: The volume set for a qualification "must fall within the range provided in the descriptor for the qualification type".
"Typically" allows flexibility for pathways, but "is not intended as justification for not applying the requirement".
The generally accepted length of a full time year is 1,200 hours.
The volume includes all teaching, learning and assessment activity: guided learning, individual study, research, workplace learning and assessment.
Developers and accreditors should be able to give a pedagogical rationale for the volume chosen.

blocks.text: The explanation also says it is usual to allocate more volume where a qualification builds on a lower level or a different discipline, or requires workplace, clinical or professional practice. For corporate programs mapped to AQF units, the same logic applies: a short course cannot credibly claim level 8 outcomes if its volume is too small to develop and assess them.

sections.heading: What has changed in the AQF recently?

blocks.text: Two changes in 2025 altered the qualification types; the level criteria themselves have not changed since 2013. The broader 2019 review has not produced a new edition as at September 2026.

items: **Undergraduate Certificate made permanent.** Introduced in response to the COVID-19 crisis, it was due to sunset on 30 June 2025. [Addendum No. 6](https://www.aqf.edu.au/publication/addendum-no-6-aqf-second-edition-january-2013-new-permanent-aqf-qualification-undergraduate) (January 2025) makes it permanent. It is a higher education qualification of six months equivalent full time study, accredited by TEQSA or by self accrediting providers, according to the [AQF Undergraduate Certificate page](https://www.aqf.edu.au/help-qualifications/undergraduate-certificate).

**Vocational Degree introduced at level 7.** [Addendum No. 7](https://www.aqf.edu.au/publication/addendum-no-7-aqf-second-edition-january-2013-vocational-degree-qualification) was endorsed by Education and Skills Ministers on 17 February 2025 and the specifications are available for use from that date. It shares the level 7 criteria with the Bachelor Degree but has its own descriptor, with learning achieved "through a combination of institution and work-based learning" and up to 6 years through a contract of training. The [AQF Vocational Degree page](https://www.aqf.edu.au/help-qualifications/vocational-degree) says these can be approved through training packages or as accredited courses accredited by ASQA, VRQA or WA TAC.

**AQF Review, 2019.** The [Department of Education](https://www.education.gov.au/reviews-and-consultations/australian-qualifications-framework-review) reports that the review's final report was released in October 2019. The Government accepted all higher education recommendations, and the aims of the VET recommendations contingent on discussion with states and territories. A cross-jurisdictional working group coordinates advice to ministers. The level structure described on this page is the one in force.

blocks.title: Check before you cite a level
blocks.text: The AQF website lists addenda as they are published. Before relying on a level or qualification type in a policy, role requirement or course approval, check the current addenda on aqf.edu.au rather than an older copy of the 2013 PDF, which does not include the Vocational Degree.

sections.heading: How should organisations use AQF levels in workplace training?

blocks.text: Organisations should use AQF levels as a calibrated vocabulary for the depth of capability a role needs, and only claim a level formally when training is accredited. Only accredited qualifications issued by authorised providers are AQF qualifications, and HESF Standard 1.5.9 prohibits describing other qualifications with AQF nomenclature.

items: **Role requirements:** specify the level of outcome a role needs (for example, level 5 application: defined responsibility in changing contexts), not just a qualification title.
**Internal programs:** write outcomes using the level criteria's verbs and contexts, and design assessment that captures the application dimension, not only knowledge recall.

**Credit and recognition:** where staff hold qualifications, [recognition of prior learning](/glossary/recognition-of-prior-learning) and credit transfer follow the AQF Qualifications Pathways Policy and the provider's own policies.

**Partnerships with providers:** when co-designing a Graduate Certificate or skill set with a university or RTO, expect the provider to test outcomes against the level criteria and the qualification type descriptor during accreditation.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each learning outcome in a program's knowledge framework with its target AQF level, its dimension (knowledge, skills or application) and the assessment point that evidences it. Reviewers can then see where outcomes claimed at a level are not actually assessed at that level, before any content is written.

faqs.q: Is a Graduate Certificate higher than a Bachelor Degree?
faqs.a: Yes, by level. A Graduate Certificate is at AQF level 8 and a Bachelor Degree at level 7. The Graduate Certificate has a much smaller volume of learning (typically 0.5 to 1 year) and builds on prior study or experience, so it is deeper in a narrow area rather than broader.

faqs.q: Is a Vocational Degree the same as a Bachelor Degree?
faqs.a: Both sit at AQF level 7 and share the level 7 criteria, with a typical volume of 3 to 4 years. The Vocational Degree has its own descriptor emphasising technical skills and a combination of institution and work-based learning, and is developed and accredited through the VET system rather than by TEQSA.

No. The AQF is national policy endorsed by Commonwealth, state and territory ministers. It gains legal effect through regulatory standards, such as HESF Standard 1.5.3, which requires higher education learning outcomes to be consistent with the qualification's AQF level, and through the accreditation of VET qualifications.

faqs.q: Can an internal corporate course be given an AQF level?
faqs.a: Not formally. Only qualifications accredited by an authorised body and issued by an authorised provider are AQF qualifications. An organisation can design internal outcomes using the AQF level criteria as a benchmark, or partner with an RTO or higher education provider to deliver accredited units or qualifications.

faqs.q: How many hours is an AQF year?
faqs.a: The AQF's volume of learning explanation states that the generally accepted length of a full time year for educational participation is 1,200 hours. That figure covers all learning and assessment activity, including individual study and workplace learning, not only scheduled teaching.
